```{r Load packages and config}

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))
source(here::here("analysis", "0-functions.R"))
```

```{r Load data}

dist_summ <- readRDS(here("data", "district_ATE_means.rds"))

dist_rand_summ <- readRDS(here("data", "district_mortality_means_by_randomization_arm.rds"))
dist_tx_summ <- readRDS(here("data", "district_mortality_means_by_treatment_group.rds"))

niger_adm2_sub <- readRDS(here("data", "niger_adm2_sub.rds"))
niger_adm2_sub <- niger_adm2_sub %>%
  left_join(dist_summ, by = c("adm2_name" = "district"))

df_all <- readRDS(here("data","grappe_mortality_data.rds"))
csi_dat_raw <- readRDS(here("data", "csi_dat.rds"))

ate_preds <- readRDS(here("data", "preds_ATE.rds")) 

```

```{r Supp table 1}

mort_ci_tbl <- dist_tx_summ %>%
  mutate(MortRate_CI = sprintf("%.1f (95%% CI: %.1f, %.1f)", MortRate, MortRate_CI_low, MortRate_CI_high)) %>%
  dplyr::select(district, isTreated_child, MortRate_CI) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = isTreated_child, values_from = MortRate_CI, names_prefix = "MortRate_")

dist_summ <- dist_summ %>%
  mutate(ATE_CI = sprintf("%.1f (95%% CI: %.1f, %.1f)", ATE, ATE_CI_low, ATE_CI_high))

dist_summ %>%
  dplyr::select(-starts_with("MortRate")) %>%
  left_join(mort_ci_tbl, by = "district") %>%
  arrange(desc(ATE)) %>%
  dplyr::select(district, ends_with("_Treatment"), ends_with("_Control"), ATE_CI) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

```


```{r Supp fig 1}

districts <- dist_summ %>%
  arrange(desc(ATE)) %>%
  pull(district) %>%
  (\(x) c("Overall", x[x != "Overall"]))()

ctrl_mort <- dist_tx_summ %>%
  dplyr::filter(isTreated_child == "Control") %>%
  dplyr::select(district, MortRate_mean) %>%
  rename(ctrl_mort = MortRate_mean)

mort_ci_dat <- bind_rows(
  dist_rand_summ,
  dist_tx_summ %>% rename(tx = isTreated_child)
) %>%
  left_join(ctrl_mort, by = "district") %>%
  dplyr::filter(tx != "Child Azithro") %>%
  mutate(tx = case_when(
    tx == "Infant Azithro" ~ "Control: Infant Azithro",
    tx == "Placebo" ~ "Control: Placebo",
    tx == "Control" ~ "**Control**",
    tx == "Treatment" ~ "**Treatment**",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),
  tx = factor(tx, 
              levels = c("Control: Infant Azithro", "Control: Placebo", "**Control**", "**Treatment**"),
              ordered = TRUE),
  district = factor(district, levels = districts, ordered = TRUE)
  )

ggplot(data = mort_ci_dat, aes(y = tx, x = MortRate, group = tx, color = tx)) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = ctrl_mort), linetype = "dashed", color = "#8B174DFF", size = 0.3) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = MortRate_CI_low, xmax = MortRate_CI_high), 
                width = 0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Control: Infant Azithro" = "#DA9FB8FF", 
                                "Control: Placebo" = "#C1447EFF", 
                                "**Control**" = "#8B174DFF", 
                                "**Treatment**" = "#6E8537FF")) +
  labs(y = "Department", x = "Mortality rate (deaths per 1000 py)") +
  xlim(c(0, 30)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y   = ggtext::element_markdown(lineheight = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ district, nrow = 3) +
  guides(color = "none")

ggsave(
  last_plot(),
  filename = here("results", "manuscript", "supp_fig1-district_mortality_rates.png"),
  width = 6,
  height = 4,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)

```

# Supp Fig 4b: predicted surfaces across the model-building sequence

A 4x4 grid of predicted surfaces: the four models of the primary model-building
sequence down the rows, the four predicted quantities across the columns. Reading
down a column shows what changes as the treatment contrast is progressively freed
to vary in space.

Note that the first two models have no treatment x location interaction, so their
rate ratio is constant by construction (0.84 in both) and their ATE surfaces vary
only through the baseline mortality rate. The flat panels in the last column of
rows 1-2 are the expected result, not a rendering failure.

```{r Supp Fig 4b surface grid}

# Row order and strip labels for the model-building sequence. Names are the
# `model` values in preds_ATE.rds; the vector doubles as the factor level order
# and as the facet labeller.
seq_labs <- c(
  "simp_krig"           = "Baseline\nspatial model",
  "gen_krig"            = "Spatial trends\nmodel",
  "gen_krig_int"        = "Linear ATE\nmodel",
  "gen_krig_spline_df3" = "Spline ATE\nmodel"
)

# rasterise_surface(): pull one model's grid column, rasterise to WGS84 and
# rename it to `value` so all four columns share plotting code. Local helper
# (used 16x below); kept here rather than in 0-functions.R because it is
# specific to the shape of this script's ate_preds object.
rasterise_surface <- function(preds_sf, model_name, colname) {
  one <- preds_sf %>%
    dplyr::filter(model == model_name) %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(colname))
  rast <- make_raster_map(one, proj_crs, global_crs, colname)
  as.data.frame(rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::rename(value = dplyr::all_of(colname))
}

# Lightweight base for a 16-panel grid: no per-panel axis text / scale bar /
# north arrow (the base_map above would repeat all of those 16 times). Model
# identity is a left-side strip; quantity is the column title.
mini_base <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 0.15) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 10),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", size = 9)
  )

# Manuscript colour scales, matching 06B-fig2-primary_maps.qmd and Supp Fig 4
# above: viridis for mortality, blue-white-red for the ATE rate difference, log
# teal-white-pink for the rate ratio. oob = squish keeps the few cells beyond a
# limit at the end colour rather than dropping them (the spline ATE surface
# dips just past -13).
scale_mort <- scale_fill_viridis_c(
  limits = c(0, 35), breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 10),
  oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA, name = "Mortality rate\n(per 1000 py)")

scale_ate <- scale_fill_gradient2(
  low = muted("dodgerblue"), mid = "white", high = muted("red"),
  midpoint = 0, limits = c(-13, 3), breaks = seq(-10, 0, by = 5),
  oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA, name = "ATE: rate difference\n(per 1000 py)")

# Linear, unlike Supp Fig 4 above, which log-transforms this scale. Nothing in
# fig 2 uses a transform, so a log bar here would be the odd one out: its ticks
# are unevenly spaced (RR = 1 lands at 63% of the bar, not the midpoint) and the
# pink arm never saturates. Asymmetric limits around the midpoint are fine and
# are what fig 2's ATE panels already do (-13 to +3 around 0).
scale_rr <- scale_fill_gradient2(
  low = muted("#009392FF"), mid = "white", high = muted("#D0587EFF"),
  midpoint = 1, limits = c(0.5, 1.5),
  breaks = seq(0.5, 1.5, by = 0.25), oob = scales::squish, na.value = NA,
  name = "Rate ratio\n(treated / control)")

# make_surface_column(): one faceted column (models down the rows) for a single
# predicted quantity, with that quantity's colour scale. `first = TRUE` keeps
# the left-side model labels; later columns drop the strip entirely and the
# extra width is given back to column 1 via plot_layout() below. Carrying an
# invisible strip in every column instead (the obvious approach) subtracts the
# width of "Spatial trends model" from all four columns, which shrinks every map
# to about half size and leaves the gutters the figure is trying to avoid.
make_surface_column <- function(colname, fill_scale, col_title, first = FALSE) {
  df <- purrr::map_dfr(names(seq_labs), function(mod) {
    rasterise_surface(ate_preds, mod, colname) %>% mutate(model = mod)
  }) %>%
    mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(seq_labs)))

  p <- mini_base +
    geom_raster(data = df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value), na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "grey30", size = 0.1) +
    facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left",
               labeller = as_labeller(seq_labs)) +
    fill_scale +
    ggtitle(col_title) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
      barheight = unit(6, "pt"), barwidth = unit(72, "pt"),
      ticks.colour = "white", frame.colour = "white"))

  if (!first) p <- p + theme(strip.text.y.left = element_blank())
  p
}

# Column titles are deliberately short: "(treated-control)" and
# "(treated/control)" would each be wider than the map beneath them, and the
# colourbar titles already carry that detail. The leading newline on the
# one-word titles keeps all four baselines on the same line.
supp_surface_grid <- (
  make_surface_column("predControl",   scale_mort, "Control\nmortality", first = TRUE) |
  make_surface_column("predTreatment", scale_mort, "Treatment\nmortality") |
  make_surface_column("ATE",           scale_ate,  "\nATE") |
  # Extra right margin on the last column: its colourbar runs to 1.5, whose
  # label otherwise clips against the edge of the saved canvas.
  (make_surface_column("rate_ratio", scale_rr, "\nRate ratio") +
     theme(plot.margin = margin(5.5, 14, 5.5, 5.5)))
) +
  # Column 1 carries the row labels, so it needs the extra width the other three
  # columns no longer spend on a strip. Panels are height-constrained at this
  # canvas size, so all four columns still get identical panel heights and the
  # rows stay aligned.
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.45, 1, 1, 1))

supp_surface_grid

ggsave(
  filename = here("results", "manuscript", "supp_fig4b-surface_grid.png"),
  plot = supp_surface_grid,
  width = 7,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

```
